name: Pippin Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: fine pippins, pared, cored, and sliced
ingredients.originalText: 8 fine pippins, pared, cored, and sliced

ingredients.name: nutmeg, and a dozen whole cloves
ingredients.originalText: 1 teaspoonful nutmeg, and a dozen whole cloves

instructions.text: Soak the bread-crumbs in the milk, cream the butter and sugar, and beat into this the yolks.
Next, adding the milk and soaked bread, stir until very smooth and light.
Put in the nutmeg and citron, and whip in the whites lightly.
Butter a deep dish, and put in your sliced apple, sprinkling each piece well with sugar, and scattering the cloves among them.
Pour the custard you have prepared over them, and bake three-quarters of an hour.
Sift powdered sugar over the top, and eat cold.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak the bread-crumbs in the milk, cream the butter and sugar, and beat into this the yolks.
2. Next, adding the milk and soaked bread, stir until very smooth and light.
3. Put in the nutmeg and citron, and whip in the whites lightly.
4. Butter a deep dish, and put in your sliced apple, sprinkling each piece well with sugar, and scattering the cloves among them.
5. Pour the custard you have prepared over them, and bake three-quarters of an hour.
6. Sift powdered sugar over the top, and eat cold.
